items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Buster incidentally had done a lot of work for me

ctx.x: Yeah. Now Booker Ervin is Dallas. You talk about this Dallas style, there's something about it. Somebody opened my eyes--when I had that incident in 1939 about Amos Woodruff--so I got to talking and needed a sax man. I was asked what kind of man and I said I definitely wanted somebody that can improvise and still have a good tone and some soul. I don't want somebody just blowing notes.
And so, we were in Dallas, Texas and Buster Bailey--I mean Buster Smith--who had been with Basie a long time, and Buster incidentally had done a lot of work for me and so

he says there's a youngster Ernie, who will fit, and I don't know what you're talking about, in Denison, Texas. So I got hold of Booker and he joined the band, and Booker just turned out to have that style that so many of them had coming from that area, a great big tone--if you remember Herschel Evans.
